intensity.Light: a SaaS tool or AI licence that works with little integration; low risk; mostly staff time.
intensity.Moderate: needs two-way links to core systems (PMS, POS, CRM) and clean data; subscription or usage fees; a human checks output.
intensity.Heavy: hardware or building-system investment, a group data platform, multi-system agents, or high legal risk (biometrics, recruitment, employee monitoring).

A1.what: Generates or summarises text, images or answers for staff. A person reads or edits the output before it is used.

A2.what: Talks directly to guests or callers through chat, voice, email or AI assistants; answers questions and takes bookings, orders or requests.

A3.what: Learns from past data to predict demand or quantities and recommends or sets a price, plan, order or rota.

A4.what: Uses what is known about a guest to tailor offers, messages or service.

A5.what: Reads documents or transactions (IDs, invoices, emails, rooming lists, statements) and turns them into records, matches or drafts; people handle exceptions.

A6.what: AI agents that carry out multi-step tasks across several systems, or the group platforms on which many AI uses run.

A7.n: On-site devices: IoT, robotics, computer vision
A7.what: AI built into physical equipment in the building (robots, sensors, cameras, building controls) that senses or acts on site.

A8.what: Watches data streams (reviews, rates, payments, networks, energy) and flags patterns, anomalies or risks for a person to act on.

A9.what: Identifies a person or informs decisions about a specific guest's identity or about staff (hiring, retention, performance).
